correctness_confidence.basis: All main claims—the centered falling-factorial sandwich, exact linear bias -(3k-1)/2, Pell-Lucas classification of adjacent collisions, zero-gap pinning of F, multiplicity-parity identity, s=1/2 Abel summation, zero-Stirling residue monotonicity, O(log x) bound for I_{2,4}(x), and Rolle degree-counting uniqueness of (2,4)—were verified line-by-line without finding any mathematical flaw.

rigor.basis: Proofs are explicit, non-asymptotic where stated, and transparent about the boundary between the 20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 kernels and the real-analytic prose proofs. Every boundary condition (e.g. x >= 6, x >= 3003, a >= 3, m >= 3) is tracked cleanly, with only minor expository compression in Theorem 2.1(2) and a parenthetical remark in Theorem 2.1(4).

novelty.basis: Resolves four concrete gaps left by Leshem and Sayag (2026): identifying the hidden quadratic overshoot barrier in unshifted diagonal sums, proving constructive Pell-Lucas classification and zero-gap two-value pinning for the Lind-Singmaster family, giving a Stirling-free proof of residue monotonicity, and proving (2,4) uniqueness via Rolle degree-counting.

significance.basis: Delivers sharp elementary improvements over deep Diophantine machinery—replacing Bombieri-Pila's x^{1/8+eps} bound on I_{2,4}(x) with an explicit O(log x) Pell bound and proving the s=1/2 divergence law unconditionally—while fixing the asymptotic bias in prior counting formulas. Its scope is a targeted refinement of [7] rather than a full attack on Singmaster's conjecture.

reproducibility.basis: The mathematical arguments in Sections 2-5 are self-contained (modulo citing Theorem 4.2 of [7] for the residue formula), and Section 6 specifies the Lean 4.36.0 module, AST-audited zero-float Python verifier with SHA-256 manifest, and 56 pytest checks. Under isolated PDF review, those external software artifacts could not be directly executed.

summary: This manuscript resolves four structural, quantitative, and Diophantine questions left open by Leshem and Sayag's recent study of Singmaster's problem, using completely elementary and constructive arguments. Key contributions include isolating an exact -(3k-1)/2 linear diagonal bias that induces an unconditional Omega((log x)^2) overshoot barrier in unshifted sums, establishing a Pell-Lucas classification of adjacent Pascal collisions with a zero-gap two-value pinning law for the Lind-Singmaster family for all x >= 3003, proving a universal multiplicity-parity dichotomy and Stirling-free residue monotonicity, and obtaining a constructive O(log x) Pellian bound for I_{2,4}(x) alongside an elegant Rolle degree-counting proof that (2,4) are the unique even-degree falling factorials admitting a quadratic polynomial representation.
strengths: Sharp, non-asymptotic discovery of the exact -(3k-1)/2 linear bias and quadratic Omega((log x)^2) overshoot barrier in unshifted diagonal sums, paired with an immediate -3k/2 correction and halved cutoff.
Clean, self-contained Pell-Lucas descent classifying all adjacent collisions and yielding an explicit zero-gap two-value pinning law for #(F intersect [1, x]) valid for every x >= 3003.

Elegant elementary proofs of the critical s = 1/2 divergence law without Bombieri-Pila/Remond, Stirling-free strict residue monotonicity via telescoping and Bernoulli's inequality, and Miska-Toth ratio-block distributions.
Exponential improvement over Bombieri-Pila for I_{2,4}(x) (O(log x) via elementary Pell descent) coupled with an exact Rolle degree-counting uniqueness theorem for (v)_2 and (v)_4.
weaknesses: In Proof (4) of Theorem 2.1, the parenthetical claim that balancing the full omitted tail at K = Theta(log x) leaves error Omega((log x / log log x)^2) is slightly ambiguous: it holds for the uncancelled bias-plus-tail bound (Theta((log x)^2)), whereas the signed difference |S_K(x) - P_2(x)| can cancel down to O(log x) near the crossover.
In Proof (2) of Theorem 2.1, dividing 2k < log_2 x + 1 + log_2(log_2 x + 2) by 2 leaves an omitted one-line verification that 1/2 < (1/2) log_2(log_2 x + 2) for x >= 6.

While Section 6 transparently delineates the Lean 4.36.0 algebraic kernels from the prose real-analytic proofs, the external Lean, Python verifier, and pytest artifacts cannot be independently executed under isolated PDF-only review.
strong_novelty_candidates: Isolation of the exact -(3k-1)/2 linear diagonal bias and unconditional Omega((log x)^2) overshoot barrier in Theorem 2.1.
Zero-gap two-value pinning law for the Lind-Singmaster Fibonacci family F valid for all x >= 3003 with simplified entropy constant c = phi^4 log(phi)/sqrt(5).
Zero-Stirling telescoping proof of strict monotonicity r_k > r_{k+1} > 1/e and limit 1/e for the Dirichlet series pole residues.

Rolle degree-counting proof of polynomial-square uniqueness for (v)_2 and (v)_4 among all even-degree falling factorials, explaining why Pellian O(log x) descent on I_{2,4}(x) cannot extend to m >= 3.
